        - heading "Objective" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Find probability of an event A given that event B has occurred.
      - article:
        - heading "The rule" [level=3]
        - text: Conditional Probability
        - strong: P(A|B) = |A ∩ B| / |B|, P(B) > 0
        - paragraph: We restrict the sample space to B and then compute the probability of A within B.
      - 'heading "Experiment: Two Dice" [level=3]'

        - paragraph: "Using the conditional probability rule:"
        - strong: P(A|B) = |A ∩ B| / |B| = 1/6

          - text: P(B) = 6/36
          - text: P(A) = 6/36

        - strong:
          - text: P(Sum is 7 | First die is 1) = 1/6
          - text: ≈ 0.1667 (16.67%)
        - paragraph: Within the 6 possible outcomes in B, 1 also belong to A.
      - heading "Misconception guard" [level=3]

        - text: Common mistake
        - paragraph: "Dividing by the total outcomes instead of the condition: |A ∩ B| / |S|."
      - article:
        - text: Why it’s wrong
        - paragraph: Conditional probability restricts the sample space to B. The denominator must be |B|, not |S|.
